hints: Look closely at the two large round airways in the centre. Notice the dark inner lining and the thick, pale, curved plates around the outside, plus the spongy alveolar tissue all around them.

Remember the cartilage rule for airways inside the lung: bronchus has cartilage plates, bronchiole has no cartilage, and trachea is never found inside lung tissue. Also compare wall thickness to separate artery from vein.
walkthrough:
**Confirm the location is the lung**

The speckled spongy background all around is alveolar lung tissue. That immediately tells you we are inside the lung, not in the neck or upper airway.

**Identify the large airways as bronchus**

The two large circular airways have a folded ciliated epithelium plus smooth muscle and obvious plates of cartilage in their walls. Cartilage present plus large size means bronchus. Bronchioles are much smaller and have no cartilage, so they are absent. Trachea has a large C-shaped ring of cartilage and is never embedded in alveolar lung tissue, so it is absent.

**Identify the two types of blood vessel**

Next to the airways you can see a small vessel with a thick muscular wall and round lumen, the artery, and a larger, thin-walled, more collapsed vessel, the vein. Both travel with the bronchus in lung tissue, so both artery and vein are present. That gives artery present, vein present, bronchioles absent, bronchus present, trachea absent, which is option A.

options.A: Correct. Artery (thick wall), vein (thin wall) and bronchus (large airway with cartilage plates in lung tissue) are all visible, while bronchioles and trachea are not.
options.B: Incorrect. It claims bronchioles and trachea are present and vein and bronchus are absent, but the large cartilage-containing airways are bronchus, not bronchioles, and trachea is not found in lung tissue.
options.C: Incorrect. It claims artery is absent and bronchioles are present, but a thick-walled artery is clearly present and no small cartilage-free bronchioles are seen.
options.D: Incorrect. It claims only bronchus and trachea are present, but both artery and vein are also present and trachea cannot be present in a section of lung alveolar tissue.
